blocks.content: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

rows: States acted as passive recipients of funds
States are active partners in the Governing Council
Empowered to allocate funds to ministries and states
Advisory think tank with no financial allocation powers
Provision for up to 2 part-time members

items: NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created via an executive resolution.
Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog has no power to allocate funds to states or ministries.
Part-time members are a maximum of 2, selected on a rotational basis from leading universities and research organizations in an ex-officio capacity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
The Governing Council comprises the Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with Legislatures, and Lt. Governors of other UTs.
Regional Councils are formed to address specific regional issues and are chaired by the Chairperson or his nominee.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister and enjoys the rank of a Cabinet Minister.
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is appointed by the Prime Minister for a fixed tenure in the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
